About.title: About me
About.eyebrow: Four years of daily automation practice
About.lead: My strength is not one specific framework, but structured problem-solving with automation, AI and testing — from the first idea to a verified result.
paragraphs: My path started with structured self-study: roughly 80 percent of the frontend roadmap on roadmap.sh, and 1st place among about 12,000 participants in the RS School / EPAM prep course. That gave me honest foundations in HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

Since then, I have worked with browser automation every day: self-employed, I built and operated Playwright-based systems with thousands of parallel sessions — selector engineering, wait strategies, proxy and fingerprint management, failure recovery. When unstable automation directly costs money, reliability becomes a habit.

Today I focus that experience on web test automation. My public e2e suite (Playwright + TypeScript, Page Object Model, API contract tests, accessibility gate) tests this very website in CI — on every push and weekly against production. I am looking for a QA / test automation role in a professional team.

motivationPoints: I turn unclear requirements into concrete work packages and functioning, tested solutions.
I do not treat AI as a black box: results are tested, questioned and improved iteratively.
I communicate knowledge gaps honestly and want to learn sound testing practices from experienced engineers.
